subject: Prod cutover: availability SLA adjustment and credits request
messages:
From: Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@evergreenhealth.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>; laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Mar 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Prod cutover — temporary SLA adjustment request

Hi Neha / Laura,

Thanks again for the tight timeline support. Our engineering team is planning a full production cutover to Redwood on the weekend of April 10–11 and we expect a higher-than-normal risk of transient service interruptions while we validate traffic shaping and routing.

We reviewed the standard SLA language but need to request a temporary exception to the uptime percentage during the two-week validation window (April 10–24). Specifically:
- Request: Allow uptime target to be adjusted from 99.95% to 99.5% for the two-week window for our production tenant only.
- Credits: Evergreen expects service credits to be calculated monthly and capped at 25% of that month’s invoice if monthly availability drops below the stated threshold. For incidents longer than 30 minutes we request per-incident credits (not just aggregated monthly).
- Latency: We will also measure API P95 and expect P95 < 300ms for user-facing endpoints during the cutover.

I attached a short note with our proposed wording (Evergreen_SLA_request.pdf). Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a two-week exception and the credit structure? If not, what counter would you propose? Procurement is copied (procurement@evergreenhealth.com) for timeline coordination — we need a signed agreement before April 6.

Thanks — Olivia

Olivia Barnes
Director, Cloud & Integrations
Evergreen Health Systems
olivia.barnes@evergreenhealth.com
+1 (415) 555-0192
From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@evergreenhealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>; marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Mar 2026 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prod cutover — temporary SLA adjustment request

Olivia — thanks for the detail and the PDF. Looping in Marcus (commercial/legal lead) and Laura (revenue ops) so we can get a compact proposal back to you.

Quick read: we can support a temporary, tenant-scoped exception but need to standardize how credits are calculated so we don’t create open-ended liability. Proposed compromise:
- Availability: Keep baseline hosted SLA at 99.95% normally. For the two-week cutover window we can agree to an adjusted availability target of 99.5% for that tenant only, effective 2026-04-10 through 2026-04-24.
- Credits: Monthly credit calculation stays in place (monthly availability bands). For the April billing period we will apply credits using the same monthly table but waive the usual 72-hour claim window for incidents occurring during the cutover; we can cap credits at 20% for that billing month.
- Per-incident: We can additionally offer per-incident credits for any single continuous outage > 90 minutes during the window (calculated using the same rates, not to exceed the monthly cap).
- Latency: We are open to contractually specifying an API P95 target for the public user endpoints. Any SLA for latency will require a mutually agreed measurement endpoint (we suggest a synthetic probe and a customer-observed metric) — we can propose language.

Next steps: I’ll ask Marcus to prepare language and a redline. If that looks acceptable we can send via DocuSign and aim to have it signed by April 5.

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
From: Tom Rios <t.rios@evergreenhealth.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>; Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@evergreenhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Mar 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prod cutover — temporary SLA adjustment request

On Sat, Mar 28, 2026 at 6:03 PM neha_kapoor@redwood.ai wrote:
> Olivia — thanks for the detail and the PDF. Looping in Marcus (commercial/legal lead) and Laura (revenue ops) so we can get a compact proposal back to you.

Appreciate the quick reply. A few clarifications from our side from the platform/ops perspective:
- The P95 latency target is critical for user experience — 300ms is our hard requirement for the endpoints serving patient-facing content. If Redwood needs a different number for internal measurement, we need a guaranteed customer-observed metric for remediation triggers.
- The per-incident >90min offer is better than 90m? We originally asked for 30 minutes because our customer impact model is sensitive to shorter outages; 90 minutes feels like too long.
- We prefer credits to be calculated per-incident and summed in the month rather than only doing a monthly bucket; that avoids a masking effect if multiple short incidents occur.

We do not want to push on the overall commercial cap too hard, but for transparency: if multiple sub-1hr outages accumulate into noticeable customer impact, a monthly-only approach means we may be under-compensated. Happy to accept a month cap, but need per-incident accounting for any outage > 30 minutes.

Can Marcus/Law provide language that preserves per-incident accounting while keeping a reasonable liability cap? Also ask: do you support providing an independent uptime feed (ping or status page) we can use to calculate downtime?

—Tom
Tom Rios
VP, Product Engineering
Evergreen Health Systems
From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Rios <t.rios@evergreenhealth.com>; Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@evergreenhealth.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>; laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Mar 2026 11:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prod cutover — temporary SLA adjustment request

Tom/Olivia — thanks. I’ve drafted a targeted redline that tries to meet both needs. Key points in the redline (attached: redlines_sla_v2.docx):
- Per-incident accounting: we will recognize individual incidents and calculate credits per-incident for any single outage > 30 minutes during the cutover window. Credits from multiple incidents will be additive subject to the monthly cap.
- Monthly cap: for April we will set a hard cap of 25% of the invoice for the month (per your ask). For future months the standard cap (20%) will apply.
- Latency SLO: We can include a P95 < 300ms objective for the specified user-facing endpoints. We will define measurement as: customer observed P95 measured via your synthetic probes against the Redwood public API endpoint listed in Appendix A. Where discrepancy exists between internal and customer probes, we will use the customer probe for remediation triggers during the cutover window only.
- Monitoring: Redwood will publish a status feed and provide an authenticated read-only endpoint (and we can also accept a third-party monitoring feed if you prefer).

A couple of guardrails: liability remains limited to service credits (no direct indemnity or consequential damages), and credits apply only to usage charges (not professional services or third-party fees).

If this matches your expectations I’ll convert to DocuSign and set the effective dates to be 2026-04-10 through 2026-04-24. I’ve also created language that removes the 72-hour claim window for incidents in that timeframe.

Attached: redlines_sla_v2.docx

—Marcus Lin
Sr. Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prod cutover — temporary SLA adjustment request

Olivia / Procurement —
Per Marcus and Neha’s threads, Redwood can accept the two-week exception with the following finalized terms:
- Availability adjustment to 99.5% for tenant ID EVG-001 for 2026-04-10 through 2026-04-24.
- Per-incident credits for any outage > 30 minutes, additive within the month.
- April monthly cap: 25% of usage charges; standard cap 20% thereafter.
- Latency SLO: P95 < 300ms as measured by Evergreen synthetic probes; customer probe is the tie-breaker for remediation during cutover.
- Monitoring: Redwood will expose an authenticated uptime feed and is open to a shared third-party monitoring configuration.

I’ve prepared the final amendment and event calendar; DocuSign link will follow. I’m attaching the cutover calendar so teams can coordinate the April 10 start.

Requested action: Procurement — please confirm the signatory and whether you need any additional procurement paperwork. Once we have confirmation I’ll issue a DocuSign packet.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Thanks Laura / Marcus / Neha — this aligns with what we need. Procurement confirms signatory contact (procurement@evergreenhealth.com) and we’ll look to return the DocuSign by April 5. One small ask: can the amendment effective date be 2026-04-09 00:00 UTC so our deployment automation has a window to flip flags before traffic begins? If that’s not possible we can accept the 10th but prefer the 9th.

Please send the DocuSign link and we’ll route internally. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Olivia
